title: Compliance Memorandum: SR-26 Cancellation Notices on Cardinal Financial Responsibility Filing Certificates
content:
**Subject:** notice to the state when the certified policy ends.

When the certified policy ends, Cardinal must tell the state. An SR-26 is transmitted for every accepted Cardinal Financial Responsibility Filing on the policy on the date the policy cancellation, nonrenewal or expiration takes effect, as switched by the certificate's settings for insured-requested cancellation, cancellation for nonpayment, company nonrenewal and expiration for an unpaid renewal.

The SR-26 takes effect the certificate's SR-26 lead days for the filing's ordering state, in calendar days, after its transmission. The certificate remains proof of financial responsibility until then, and lapses on that date.

A driver whose certificate lapsed needs a new filing where the certificate requires a new filing after a lapse, and the state may suspend the driver's license. Cardinal does not intervene in state suspensions.

## Timeline

| Point | What holds |
|---|---|
| Policy cancellation, nonrenewal or expiration takes effect | SR-26 transmitted that date for each accepted filing on the policy |
| From transmission until the SR-26 effective date | Certificate is still proof of financial responsibility (status cancel-notified) |
| SR-26 effective date (transmission date plus the state's lead days) | Certificate lapses |
| After the lapse | A new filing is needed; any license suspension is the state's matter |

## Hypothetical illustration

A policy carrying an accepted certificate filed with an ordering state whose lead time is 10 days is cancelled effective 1 June. The SR-26 is transmitted on 1 June and takes effect on 11 June. From 1 June to 10 June the certificate is still proof of financial responsibility; on 11 June it lapses. The dates and the lead time are chosen for illustration.
